content.overview: Dividend shall be declared or paid by a company for any financial year only out of the profits of the company for that year arrived at after providing for depreciation, or out of profits of any previous financial year or years arrived at after providing for depreciation and remaining undistributed, or out of both, or out of money provided by the Central Government or a State Government for the payment of dividend in pursuance of a guarantee, subject to the conditions in section 123 and the applicable rules. Dividend, including interim dividend, is to be deposited in a separate scheduled-bank account within five days of declaration and paid within thirty days subject to section 127.
content.glance: Dividend only out of profits after depreciation (or Government money for that purpose), with deposit within five days and payment within thirty days subject to section 127.
content.study:
## Section 123 — Declaration of dividend

**Source rule.** Dividend may be declared or paid only out of profits for that year after providing for depreciation, or out of previous years' profits after depreciation remaining undistributed, or out of both, or out of money provided by the Central or a State Government for payment of dividend. Depreciation under Schedule II must be provided. Dividend cannot be declared from unrealised gains or revaluation reserves. A company in default of deposits cannot declare dividend during the default.

**Interim dividend.** May be declared from surplus in the profit and loss account or from current-year profits, subject to the section.

**Deposit and payment.** Dividend, including interim dividend, is to be deposited in a scheduled bank in a separate account within five days of declaration. It must be paid or the warrant posted within thirty days under section 127, failing which the company and directors face consequences, with the exceptions in section 127.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Source of dividend
sections.body: Profits after depreciation (current or previous years or both), or Government money provided for that purpose. Not from unrealised or revaluation items.

sections.heading: Deposit and payment
sections.body: Separate scheduled-bank account within five days of declaration; payment within thirty days subject to section 127.

examples.body: An upward revaluation is not a fund for dividend. Educational illustration.

examples.body: Declared dividend must move to a separate scheduled-bank account within five days. Educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: Can interim dividend be paid from previous-year losses if the current quarter is profitable?
hypotheticals.analysis: Interim dividend must fit the source rules in section 123, including the current-profit and no-loss conditions stated in the section. A loss in the preceding quarter may restrict the rate as the section provides.

misconceptions.trap: Declaring dividend from revaluation reserves or unrealised gains.
misconceptions.correction: Section 123 does not permit declaration from unrealised gains or revaluation reserves.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Out of what may a company declare dividend under section 123?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Out of profits for the year after depreciation, or previous years' profits after depreciation remaining undistributed, or both, or out of Government money provided for that purpose, subject to the section and rules.
